title: Given a string, partition it so that every substring of the partition is a palindrome, and return all possible palindrome partitionings. Explain the backtracking technique that cuts the string at each position and only recurses when the prefix is a palindrome.
shortTitle: Palindrome Partitioning (All Ways to Split a String into Palindromes)
keyPoints: Use backtracking from a start index, trying every end position to form a prefix.
Only recurse when the prefix from start to end is a palindrome, pruning invalid cuts early.
A partition is complete when the start index reaches the end of the string.
Check palindromes with a two-pointer comparison from both ends of the substring.
Precompute a palindrome DP table to make each palindrome check O(1) instead of O(n).
Record a fresh copy of the current partition list when a complete partition is found.
The search is exponential in the worst case, bounded by the number of valid palindromic partitions.

s1_definition.oneliner: From each start position, try every prefix, recurse only on palindromic prefixes, and record a partition when the whole string is consumed.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Palindrome partitioning** – enumerates every way to cut a string into pieces where each piece reads the same forwards and backwards.
- **Backtracking with pruning** – from the current start index, try every end position; only recurse when the prefix is a palindrome.
- **Completion condition** – a partition is complete when the start index equals the string length.
- **Palindrome check** – either a two-pointer O(n) check or a precomputed O(1) lookup from a DP table.
- **Exponential output** – the number of valid partitions can be exponential, so the algorithm is necessarily exponential.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, a reference token must be split into symmetric segments for a legacy validator. Rajesh tries cutting after the first character, after the second, and so on. Whenever a piece is symmetric, he accepts it and recursively splits what remains. Every complete split where all pieces are symmetric is recorded.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
Backtracking tree for "AAB":

  backtrack(start=0, current=[])
  |
  |-- prefix "A" (palindrome)
  |   backtrack(start=1, current=["A"])
  |   |
  |   |-- prefix "A" (palindrome)
  |   |   backtrack(start=2, current=["A","A"])
  |   |   |
  |   |   |-- prefix "B" (palindrome)
  |   |   |   backtrack(start=3, current=["A","A","B"])
  |   |   |   start==3 -> RECORD ["A","A","B"]
  |   |   |
  |   |   |-- prefix "AB" (NOT palindrome) -> PRUNE
  |   |
  |   |-- prefix "AB" (NOT palindrome) -> PRUNE
  |
  |-- prefix "AA" (palindrome)
  |   backtrack(start=2, current=["AA"])
  |   |
  |   |-- prefix "B" (palindrome)
  |   |   backtrack(start=3, current=["AA","B"])
  |   |   start==3 -> RECORD ["AA","B"]
  |
  |-- prefix "AAB" (NOT palindrome) -> PRUNE

  Result: [["A","A","B"], ["AA","B"]]

  Key: non-palindrome prefixes are pruned immediately,
  avoiding recursion into their subtrees.
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Palindrome Partitioning enumerates every way to cut a string into pieces where each piece is a palindrome. You solve it with backtracking from a start index. From the current start, you try every end position to form a prefix, and only when that prefix is a palindrome do you accept it into the current partition and recurse on the remainder. When the start index reaches the end of the string, the current list of pieces is a complete valid partition and you record a fresh copy.

The key optimization is that you recurse only on palindromic prefixes, which prunes the enormous number of invalid cuts immediately rather than building them and rejecting them later. A two-pointer palindrome check runs in O(n) per call, and the same substrings may be tested across different branches. Precomputing a palindrome DP table makes each check O(1), removing a linear factor from each node in the recursion tree.

The overall complexity is still exponential because it is bounded by the number of valid palindromic partitions, which can be exponential for strings like `"AAAA..."`. But the palindrome-only pruning and the DP precomputation ensure that no work is wasted on invalid branches. Recording a fresh copy of the current list at each complete partition is mandatory to avoid sharing a mutable reference across all results.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh used this to generate all valid symmetric segmentations of reference tokens for a legacy validator test suite. The backtracking produced every valid split, and the palindrome pruning kept the search efficient for tokens with few palindromic substrings. The precomputed palindrome table was reused across multiple tokens.

Remember one sentence: from each start, try every prefix, recurse only if it is a palindrome, and record the partition when the whole string is consumed.
